passage: The launch was two hours away when Nitin announced on the group call, "The missing file is Varun's fault, as usual." Every camera seemed to turn towards Varun. His stomach dropped, and a sarcastic reply rose to his lips: "Sure, I also caused the weather." He swallowed it. "The file was uploaded yesterday at 6 pm," he said evenly. "I'll put the upload record in the thread now." He did, then messaged Nitin privately: "Can we check the access log together after launch?" The launch went ahead using a backup copy. That evening Varun wrote down the times and sent a short factual summary to the project manager, copying Nitin. Nitin didn't reply, but the blame stopped.

qa.q: At what time did Varun say the file was uploaded?
What was Varun feeling when Nitin blamed him on the call?
qa.a: His stomach dropped and a sarcastic reply rose to his lips, so he was stung and angry, but he swallowed it.

qa.q: What made Varun's response better than a sarcastic reply?
qa.a: He kept to facts, posted the upload record and took the rest to a private message and the project manager.

qa.q: How might Nitin have felt with the launch two hours away?
qa.a: Probably under pressure and anxious, which may explain the blame though not excuse it; Nitin's silence afterwards shows nothing certain.

grounding: A young professional facing blame keeps to facts, avoids a public rebuttal, documents events and escalates through the proper channel, under time pressure.

passage: Neelam had a way of saying "Gargi must have forgotten" in front of others whenever a report was late. The third time, at the Tuesday huddle in the Pune office, Gargi felt heat in her face and wanted to say something biting. Instead she said, "The report was due Friday, and I put it in the shared folder on Thursday at four. I'll show you the timestamp." Neelam changed the subject. After the huddle Gargi wrote a dated list of the three incidents with the folder times and emailed her team manager: "I'd like to talk about how late reports are being attributed. The details are attached." The manager set up a call with both of them for Thursday. Gargi went home tired, but she kept her sarcasm to herself all week.

qa.q: When did Gargi put the report in the shared folder?
What was Gargi feeling at the huddle, and what did she do with it?
qa.a: She was angry, with heat in her face and an urge to say something biting, but she calmly stated the timestamp instead.

qa.q: Why was documenting the incidents useful?
qa.a: The dated list and timestamps gave the manager facts and made it a proper-channel issue rather than a personal fight.

qa.q: How might Neelam have seen Gargi's timestamp?
qa.a: Neelam changed the subject, which suggests she was caught off guard or uncomfortable, though Neelam may not have meant harm.

grounding: A young professional facing repeated blame keeps to facts, documents the incidents and escalates to the manager without retaliatory sarcasm.
